name: Ka
label: Iron Works
lede: A fire captain who quit rap, came back in his thirties, sold his best album off the sidewalk outside a dead record store, and built his records on almost no drums.

eras.title: Hull Street, Brownsville
eras.text: Kaseem Ryan grows up in a Brownsville row house in the crack years and starts writing rhymes as a kid. The city's rap radio is his school.

years.cap: Brownsville, Brooklyn, where Ka was born and stayed.
years.src: Wikipedia: Ka (rapper) · The FADER: New York Rap's Greatest Living Treasure
years.h: Kaseem Ryan is born in Brownsville, Brooklyn
years.p: He grows up in his family's house on Hull Street. His father is in prison until Ka is about six.
years.xp:
Wikipedia gives his birth date as August 11, 1972. The FADER found him at 44 still tied to the neighborhood: poverty, gangs, and then crack breaking up whatever community there had been.

Ka told the magazine that the corners where people now buy coffee were once a different kind of crazy. Everything he later wrote, from the chess metaphors to the gospel samples, starts on those blocks.

years.src: The FADER: New York Rap's Greatest Living Treasure · Wikipedia: Ka (rapper)
years.h: Ka's cousin Dion hands him $1,000 to start a rap career
years.p: The FADER dates the gift to 1989, when Ka was 17 and already rhyming.
years.xp: Wikipedia dates his earliest recorded song to 1989 or 1990. He went on to attend City College of New York, where he met Mr. Voodoo, later of [[Natural Elements|b2230eb0-1785-4386-a04f-c6f216d55352]].

eras.title: The weak one in the group
eras.text: Ka gets in the room with real New York rap, including a group a major label wants, and walks away from it. He then spends years on an EP nobody buys.

years.src: Wikipedia: Natural Elements (hip-hop group) · The FADER: New York Rap's Greatest Living Treasure · Wikipedia: Ka (rapper)
years.h: He joins [[Natural Elements|b2230eb0-1785-4386-a04f-c6f216d55352]] under Charlemagne in the Bronx
years.p: The crew forms in Baychester under the producer Charlemagne and his Fortress label. Ka is one of six original members, billed as K A.
years.xp: Wikipedia's band page puts the start in 1993 and lists the first lineup as Mr. Voodoo, L Swift, Ka, Howie Smalls, G-Blass and The InTIMidator. His own page says he joined in 1994. The group got noticed freestyling on Stretch and Bobbito's radio show, where Ka also met his future wife, Mimi Valdes.

q: I was the weak one in the group.
years.src: The FADER: New York Rap's Greatest Living Treasure · Wikipedia: Natural Elements (hip-hop group) · Red Bull Music Academy Daily: Ka, No Breaks Needed
years.h: Ka leaves Natural Elements before the Tommy Boy deal
years.p: He decides he is holding the group back and quits. The group goes on to sign with Tommy Boy without him.
years.xp:
Ka told the FADER he left feeling outmatched by his groupmates, and said the same at a Red Bull Music Academy lecture. Def Jam had shown interest in the crew, but no deal came of it.

Natural Elements released the single "2 Tons/Live It Up" on Tommy Boy's Black Label in 1998, then saw their debut album shelved by the label.

years.src: Wikipedia: Ka (rapper) · The FADER: New York Rap's Greatest Living Treasure
years.h: Nightbreed: Ka and his friend Kev start a duo
years.p: Ka and Kev, a rapper he had known since childhood, form Nightbreed. They try to get signed for four years.
years.xp: Wikipedia dates the duo to 1995. The FADER says Ka could not land a record deal by 1999 and stopped.

years.src: Red Bull Music Academy Daily: Ka, No Breaks Needed · Wikipedia: Ka (rapper)
years.h: 2 Roads Out the Ghetto, Nightbreed's only record
years.p: A three-track 12-inch on Fortress Entertainment, Charlemagne's label. It sells nowhere, and Ka takes it as an answer.
years.xp: Red Bull Music Academy describes it as an independent release that went nowhere. It is the last thing Ka puts out for a decade.

eras.title: Twenty years of nights
eras.text: Ka quits rap for the fire department and does not look back until his wife talks him into it. He works 24-hour shifts for two decades.

years.cap: Ka served 20 years with the FDNY.
years.src: The FADER: New York Rap's Greatest Living Treasure · Wikipedia: Ka (rapper) · CBS New York: Underground Brooklyn rapper Kaseem Ryan dead at 52
yt: Brownsville KA: how a firefighter became a rapper
years.h: Ka quits rap to become a New York City firefighter
years.p: He wants structure and community. He stays in the FDNY for 20 years and is a first responder on September 11, 2001.
years.xp:
The FADER says he formally quit music in 2003 too, and that the decision hurt: he had spent years honing a skill "for absolutely nothing." Wikipedia says he worked in both the Bronx and Brooklyn and was promoted to captain at Engine Co. 235 in Bedford-Stuyvesant in 2009.

The job stays in the background of everything he does. As he later put it, he never wanted to be "The Rapping Captain."

years.src: The FADER: New York Rap's Greatest Living Treasure · Red Bull Music Academy Daily: Ka, No Breaks Needed
years.h: His wife, Mimi Valdes, talks him back to the booth
years.p: She hears something worth saving in what he has been writing. He starts recording again around 2005.
years.xp: The FADER puts the return at about 2005. Red Bull Music Academy has him saying it took a year of digging for records to find 15 beats worth rhyming on, and sometimes two months to write one verse.

eras.title: Iron Works
eras.text: Ka runs his own label out of a firehouse schedule. He gets a GZA feature, then sells his best record by hand on a Manhattan sidewalk.

years.src: Wikipedia: Ka (rapper) · Red Bull Music Academy Daily: Ka, No Breaks Needed · CBS New York: Underground Brooklyn rapper Kaseem Ryan dead at 52
years.h: Iron Works arrives, and GZA hears it
years.p: Ka's debut is self-released on his own label, Iron Works. GZA invites him onto "Firehouse" from the Wu-Tang rapper's album Pro Tools.
years.xp: Wikipedia and Red Bull Music Academy date the album to 2008. CBS New York gives 2007. CBS also says he handed out about 1,000 CDs for free at first.

years.src: Wikipedia: Ka (rapper) · The FADER: New York Rap's Greatest Living Treasure
years.h: Ka is promoted to captain at Engine 235 in Bed-Stuy
years.p: He now runs a company of firefighters by day. The day job stays quiet for years.

years.src: Complex: Ka Tells the Stories Behind the Self-Directed Videos
years.h: Ka starts directing a video a month for his next album
years.p: The first, "Cold Facts," posts September 17, 2011. He shoots between 2 and 4 AM in Brownsville project buildings, rooftops and precincts.
years.xp: Complex tallied the series: one clip roughly every month through "Born King N.Y." in August 2012. Ka said it was the peacefulness of those hours that he liked.

years.src: Albumism: Ka's Grief Pedigree Turns 10 · Complex: Ka Tells the Stories Behind the Self-Directed Videos
years.h: Grief Pedigree: Ka, alone, at his best
years.p: He makes it entirely himself and puts [[Roc Marciano|9b14ef6d-119b-47b8-9d06-fc72901451e2]] on one track, "Iron Age." Albumism later calls it one of the best albums of the 2010s.
years.xp:
Ka directed and edited videos for the songs, mostly in black and white and shot around Brownsville and New York. Albumism credits it with shaping a generation of gritty, sparse New York rap, Griselda included.

The friendship with Roc Marciano dated from their work on GZA's Pro Tools.

years.cap: Fat Beats' former Sixth Avenue address, where Ka sold Grief Pedigree.
years.src: Albumism: Ka's Grief Pedigree Turns 10 · Red Bull Music Academy Daily: Ka, No Breaks Needed
years.h: Ka sells Grief Pedigree from the sidewalk outside Fat Beats
years.p: The shop has been closed since September 2010. Ka stands at its old Sixth Avenue address and peddles the CD himself.
years.xp: A producer named Preservation picked up a copy there, and told Ka that Mos Def had been talking about his music. That meeting led to Days with Dr. Yen Lo. Ka told Red Bull Music Academy he will always stand outside and peddle the art.

eras.title: Chess, film noir and a tabloid
eras.text: Ka turns drumless rap into a concept series: chess, then a Cold War thriller, then samurai. Then the New York Post shows up.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Night's Gambit
years.h: The Night's Gambit: the chess album
years.p: Ka produces all of it at The End studio in Greenpoint, with Roc Marciano appearing on "Soap Box." Pitchfork gives it 8.0.
years.xp: Every track is bookended with samples, and the record runs just under 40 minutes. Spin ranked it No. 8 for 2013, and The Needle Drop put it at No. 9.

years.src: Wikipedia: Ka (rapper) · Red Bull Music Academy Daily: Ka, No Breaks Needed
years.h: Ka and Preservation team up on the 1200 B.C. EP
years.p: The first release from the pair that met outside the old Fat Beats.

years.src: Wikipedia: Days with Dr. Yen Lo · Red Bull Music Academy Daily: Ka, No Breaks Needed
years.h: Days with Dr. Yen Lo, with Preservation
years.p: A Manchurian Candidate record: Ka narrates, DJ Preservation directs. Pitchfork gives it 8/10, and Earl Sweatshirt calls it his album of 2015.
years.xp: The two named themselves after Khigh Dhiegh's Dr. Yen Lo in the 1962 film, and cut soundbites into the album rather than retelling the plot. It took about two years, and Ka launched it at Other Music in the East Village. Rolling Stone ranked it No. 9 on its 40 best rap albums list and Stereogum No. 19.

years.src: Wikipedia: Honor Killed the Samurai
years.h: Honor Killed the Samurai turns bushido into autobiography
years.p: Ten tracks in 36 minutes, all produced by Ka. Pitchfork gives it 8.0 and calls his voice hushed but vicious.

years.big: "KA should be celebrated as a New York treasure."
years.src: Stereogum: El-P Defends Ka · The FADER: New York Rap's Greatest Living Treasure
years.h: The New York Post outs the "anti-cop" rapper fire captain
years.p: [[El-P|d9241f5b-721a-4e08-a25a-acd83ed878cc]] and [[Killer Mike|47864525-aea7-439a-800f-17c57e51cbcc]] respond on social media. Ka's own reply is one line about love and hate.
years.xp:
The Post ran it under the headline "FLAME THROWER: FDNY captain moonlights as anti-cop rapper," quoting lyrics from songs four years old. According to Stereogum, it also printed his station assignment, his pay and what he paid for his house.

El-P, who quoted the "New York treasure" line, went on: "perhaps if a rapper spends his days saving people from death by fire you should assume his character is strong." Ka's tweet: "With love comes hate...can't have one without the other."

eras.title: Patron saints of Iron Works
eras.text: The series keeps coming: a duo record, then four albums in three years. Younger rappers start naming him as the standard.

years.src: Wikipedia: Ka (rapper)
years.h: Ka and Animoss release Orpheus vs. the Sirens
years.p: A collaboration as Hermit and the Recluse on the Obol for Charon label.

years.src: Wikipedia: Descendants of Cain (album)
years.h: Descendants of Cain, a 33-minute record about fear and regeneration
years.p: [[Roc Marciano|9b14ef6d-119b-47b8-9d06-fc72901451e2]] produces and raps on "Sins of the Father." Pitchfork gives it 8.1 and ranks it No. 35 of 2020.
years.xp: Paul A. Thompson's Pitchfork review says the album includes some of the most striking writing of Ka's career. Metacritic's average across four reviews was 85, and Stereogum placed it No. 10 on its 2020 list.

years.src: Wikipedia: A Martyr's Reward
years.h: A Martyr's Reward brings in [[Navy Blue|304c731f-ea4f-407c-b4fc-65131b1b2b37]] and Joi
years.p: Pitchfork gives it 8.3 and ranks it No. 48 of 2021. Ka produces most of the 13 tracks himself.

years.src: Wikipedia: Ka (rapper)
years.h: Ka drops Languish Arts and Woeful Studies on the same day
years.p: Two albums, one date, September 16, 2022, both on Iron Works.

eras.title: The Thief Next to Jesus
eras.text: Ka's last album is his most direct about faith. Two months after it comes out, he is gone.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Thief Next to Jesus · Album of the Year: Ka, The Thief Next to Jesus · Stereogum: Ka's New Album The Thief Next To Jesus Is Streaming Now
yt: The Needle Drop reviews The Thief Next to Jesus
years.h: The Thief Next to Jesus: Ka's last album, about church
years.p: Pitchfork's Matthew Ritchie gave it 8.1 and ranked it No. 24 of 2024. The 14 tracks run 35 minutes and lean on gospel samples.
years.xp:
Ritchie wrote that Ka parses and critiques the Black American connection to Christianity. Mastering was by Michael Fossenkemper and mixing by Scotty Hard, with Preservation on extra Pro Tools editing. Anthony Fantano scored it 9/10; Complex placed it No. 6 of 2024, Stereogum No. 18, The Fader No. 12.

Release was on Iron Works: first as $20 WAV downloads, then streaming about a month later. Ka directed the videos for "Such Devotion" and "Borrowed Time" himself.

years.src: Stereogum: Ka's New Album The Thief Next To Jesus Is Streaming Now
years.h: A one-day pop-up shop on Charlton Street
years.p: Ka sells vinyl at $100 and CDs at $20 at 104 Charlton St. in Manhattan, from 1 to 9 PM.

q: I never wanted to be 'The Rapping Captain.'
years.src: Stereogum: Ka Dead At 52 · CBS New York: Underground Brooklyn rapper Kaseem Ryan dead at 52 · Wikipedia: Ka (rapper)
yt: Ka's last interview before his death
years.h: Ka dies at 52, two months after his last album
years.p: His family announces it on Instagram on October 14. The cause of death was not announced.
years.xp:
Wikipedia gives October 12, 2024 as the date. Stereogum says the family's message said he died unexpectedly. CBS New York also quoted the FDNY: "Capt. Ryan served the FDNY and the people of the city with distinction for 20 years." He is survived by his wife, his mother and his sister.

CBS and Stereogum both noted his 20 years on the job and his work as a first responder on September 11.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Thief Next to Jesus · Album of the Year: Ka, The Thief Next to Jesus
years.h: Pitchfork puts The Thief Next to Jesus at No. 24
years.p: Complex, The Needle Drop and Passion of the Weiss rank it higher. Album of the Year's reviews page lists Vulture at No. 3.

eras.title: After the Thief
eras.text: The record keeps getting found. Friends release verses he left behind.

years.src: Wikipedia: Ka (rapper)
years.h: Che Noir's Seeds in Babylon carries a Ka interlude
years.p: One of the verses released after his death. Navy Blue's 2026 track "Circa" also credits him.
